Infeasible and unbounded models

Source: vignettes/infeasible-models.Rmd
infeasible-models.Rmd
library(optcompR)

optcompR describes an optimization problem once, as variables, expressions, constraints and an objective, and then classifies it, chooses a capable solver A model can fail to have an optimal solution because no point satisfies the constraints (infeasible) or because the objective improves without limit (unbounded). Some solvers can only say that one of the two holds.

Detecting infeasibility 

m <- opt_model()
x <- opt_variable(m, "x", dim = 2, lower = 0)
opt_constraint(m, x[1] + x[2] <= 3, name = "cap")
opt_constraint(m, x[1] >= 2, name = "min_a")
opt_constraint(m, x[2] >= 2, name = "min_b")
opt_objective(m, x[1] + x[2])
r <- opt_solve(m)
opt_status(r)
#> [1] "infeasible"
opt_has_solution(r)
#> [1] FALSE
opt_value(r, x)
#> Warning: The result has no primal solution (status 'infeasible').
#> [1] NA NA

Values are NA when there is no primal point, rather than the solver’s internal iterate.

Locating the conflict with elastic constraints

Adding nonnegative slack to each suspect row and minimizing the total slack finds the smallest change that restores feasibility.

e <- opt_model()
x <- opt_variable(e, "x", dim = 2, lower = 0)
s <- opt_variable(e, "s", dim = 3, lower = 0)
opt_constraint(e, x[1] + x[2] <= 3 + s[1], name = "cap")
opt_constraint(e, x[1] >= 2 - s[2], name = "min_a")
opt_constraint(e, x[2] >= 2 - s[3], name = "min_b")
opt_objective(e, sum(s))
re <- opt_solve(e)
setNames(opt_value(re, s), c("cap", "min_a", "min_b"))
#>   cap min_a min_b 
#>     0     1     0

The total violation is 1: either capacity rises by 1 or one minimum falls by 1.

Exact proofs with Z3

Floating point solvers declare infeasibility within tolerances. For linear models, opt_z3_check() decides feasibility exactly (see vignette("exact-certificates")):

opt_z3_check(m)$status
#> [1] "unsat"

Unbounded models 

u <- opt_model("max")
y <- opt_variable(u, "y", lower = 0)
opt_constraint(u, y >= 1)
opt_objective(u, y)
opt_status(opt_solve(u))
#> [1] "unbounded"

OSQP certifies dual infeasibility, which does not prove the primal problem feasible, so optcompR reports infeasible_or_unbounded for it:

opt_status(opt_solve(u, solver = "osqp"))
#> [1] "infeasible_or_unbounded"
